plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Tiny golden-yellow flower clusters sit at the center of brilliant, petal-like bracts. Those bracts blaze scarlet across the hillsides and gardens of its homeland, and they are the flower most associated with Christmas.
plants.bloomingSeason: November to December (short-day flowering, peaking around Christmas)
plants.location: Southern Mexico, its native range, and warm gardens in the tropics and subtropics
plants.funFact: The showy 'petals' are really modified leaves called bracts. The true flowers are the small yellow cups, called cyathia, at their center.

plants.name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
plants.description: This Australian native shrub is covered in small creamy flowers in early summer. As each flower fades, its sepals swell and turn rich red, so the whole bush glows with festive color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Flowers open from about December, with the red calyces developing through the holiday season
plants.location: Eastern Australia, from the Sydney sandstone region and coastal New South Wales to gardens in Canberra
plants.funFact: The red 'petals' are actually enlarged calyces, the sepals, which keep growing after the true flowers drop.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This graceful evergreen shrub is covered in open, softly scented blooms with golden stamens just as most gardens fall quiet. Its flowers light up winter hedges and shaded paths.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, from about October or November through December and into January
plants.location: Native to southern Japan and widely grown in temperate gardens of Japan, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are close relatives of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis.
